title: What is the square root of 1936, without long multiplication?
description: The square root of one thousand nine hundred thirty six is trapped between two known squares, and the last digit and one test square narrow it down. Keeko doubts the narrowing, because the last digit alone seems to point to forty six.
teaching_notes: One idea: trap the root between known squares, use the last digit for the candidates, and test the middle square. Watch for students who pick a candidate from the last digit alone and never test it.

video_script.why: The child finds a square root by trapping it between squares, using the last digit, and testing the middle square.
video_script.substitution: Find two squares around the number, list the candidates from the last digit, and test the square in between.
video_script.anchor: a square with area one thousand nine hundred thirty six and a side marked with a question
video_script.wrong_answer: the root must be forty six
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko picks forty six from the last digit alone, because six also ends forty six. Forty four also ends in a number whose square ends in six, so a test is needed, and forty six squared is too big.
video_script.payoff_line: The square root of one thousand nine hundred thirty six is forty four

final_answer.spoken: the square root of one thousand nine hundred thirty six is forty four

maths_rules: a square ending in 6 has a root ending in 4 or 6, so the root is 44 or 46
video_script.design: One idea: trap, list, test. Wrong idea: the last digit alone picks the root. The square stays on the stage and the three steps sit on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='side'/>The square root of a number is the side of a square with that area.
<bookmark mark='known'/>If a smaller and a larger square are known, our side must fit between their sides.
<bookmark mark='trap'/>That traps the root without any long multiplication.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number is one thousand nine hundred thirty six.

beats.on_screen: To find: the square root of 1936

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find its square root.

beats.on_screen: 40² = 1600 and 50² = 2500, so 1600 < 1936 < 2500 and the root is between 40 and 50

marks.between: 1936 is placed between them, and the root is marked between 40 and 50

narration: <bookmark mark='low'/>Step one, trap the root between two squares we know.
<bookmark mark='high'/>Forty squared is one thousand six hundred, and fifty squared is two thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='between'/>Our number sits between them, so the root is between forty and fifty.

beats.on_screen: 1936 ends in 6, so the root ends in 4 or 6: 44 or 46

marks.digit: the last digit 6 of 1936 is circled
marks.cand: the two candidates 44 and 46 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='digit'/>Step two, look at the last digit, which is six.
A square ends in six only when its root ends in four or six.
<bookmark mark='cand'/>The root is forty four or forty six.

beats.on_screen: test the middle: 45² = (40 + 5)(40 + 5) = 1600 + 400 + 25 = 2025, and 2025 > 1936, so the root is below 45

marks.below: 2025 > 1936 is written and the root is marked below 45

narration: <bookmark mark='test'/>Step three, test forty five in the middle.
Write forty five as forty plus five, and multiply it by itself.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>That gives one thousand six hundred, then four hundred, then twenty five, which is two thousand twenty five.
<bookmark mark='below'/>This is bigger than our number, so the root is below forty five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The root is below forty five, so it is forty four.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Check it, forty four times forty four is one thousand nine hundred thirty six.
The square root of one thousand nine hundred thirty six is forty four.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says 46 from the last digit; 46² = 2116 is written, it is bigger than 1936, and the bubble is struck through

marks.fix: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the root must be forty six, because six also ends forty six.
<bookmark mark='big'/>But four also gives a square ending in six, so the last digit cannot choose.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Forty six squared is two thousand one hundred sixteen, which is too big, so the test decides.
